test_cases.title: Valid card — subscription activates successfully
test_cases.precondition: User is logged in; Stripe test mode is active in staging
steps: Enter any future expiry date and CVC
test_cases.expected: Payment processes, subscription status changes to 'Premium', confirmation email sent
test_cases.actual: Payment processed successfully; subscription updated to Premium; confirmation email received within 30 seconds

test_cases.title: Invalid card number — inline validation error shown
test_cases.precondition: User is on the subscription payment page
test_cases.expected: Inline validation error 'Your card number is invalid' appears below the card field
test_cases.actual: Stripe's validation correctly displayed 'Your card number is invalid' in red below the field

test_cases.title: Expired card — payment declined with clear message
test_cases.precondition: User is on the subscription payment page
steps: Enter Stripe test card for declined payment: 4000 0000 0000 0002
Enter a future expiry date and valid CVC
test_cases.expected: Payment is declined; error message 'Your card was declined' is shown to the user
test_cases.actual: Payment declined correctly; error message displayed; user stays on payment page

test_cases.title: Payment page load time — must be under 2 seconds on slow 3G
test_cases.precondition: Browser DevTools Network throttled to Slow 3G (400 kbps down)
steps: Measure time until the payment form is fully interactive (Stripe card field is focusable)
test_cases.expected: Payment form is fully interactive within 2 seconds on Slow 3G
test_cases.actual: Payment form took 6.8 seconds to become interactive on Slow 3G. The Stripe.js library is loaded synchronously, blocking render.
test_cases.notes: Chrome Lighthouse score for this page: Performance 31/100. Main culprit is synchronous Stripe.js load in <head>.

bugs.title: Payment page render-blocks on slow connections due to synchronous Stripe.js load
bugs.description: The Stripe.js library is loaded via a synchronous <script> tag in the <head> of the payment page. This blocks page rendering entirely until Stripe.js finishes downloading, which takes 4-7 seconds on Slow 3G. Users on mobile data in poor coverage areas cannot complete purchases.
steps: Open Chrome DevTools, Network tab, set throttle to 'Slow 3G'
Navigate to the subscription upgrade page
Observe that the page remains blank for 4-7 seconds
Note the Stripe.js request blocking rendering in the waterfall
bugs.expected: Page content renders immediately; Stripe.js loads asynchronously after initial paint
bugs.actual: Page is blank for ~6 seconds until Stripe.js completes loading
bugs.notes: Fix: move Stripe.js to async load or use <script defer>. This is a P0 for mobile users in low-connectivity regions.

bugs.title: Stripe.js not cached — reloaded on every page visit
bugs.description: The Stripe.js script does not have correct cache headers, causing the browser to re-download it on every page visit rather than serving it from cache. This compounds the slow load time issue.
steps: Visit the payment page once to prime the cache
bugs.expected: Stripe.js is served with a long max-age cache header and returns 304 on subsequent visits
bugs.actual: Stripe.js returns 200 with no meaningful cache headers on every visit
bugs.notes: This is a CDN/hosting configuration issue. Assigned to DevOps team. ETA: 2026-05-17.
